findings.title: The opening name frames the action chain
findings.claim: The name named in the basmala places the following intervention under Allah's agency: as the pericope moves from “your Lord acted” through the frustrated plan, the sent birds, the cast stones, and the final transformation, the opening reads as a frame for whose act the sequence narrates.
findings.mechanism: The focus noun ismi carries the ordinary sense of name or designation, and Allah is the exclusive divine proper name in the invocation. In 105:1–5 that opening is followed by a continuous chain of divine action; their contact makes the designation scope the sequence as an attributional frame.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can carry “in the name of Allah” into the following actions, so the basmala stays attached to the narrated scene rather than sitting apart from it.
findings.containment: This is a pericope-level relation between the opening formula and the supplied action chain. It does not make every later detail an act of mercy, specify one motive, or identify a protected beneficiary; other grounded readings remain live.

epistemic.reason: A trusted cross-run finding and a legacy reader walk describe the same frame, but the scope from a prefatory formula to later clauses is interpretive rather than syntactically stated.
